backlog.spec: Set WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.3. For short runs this probably matters little, but test the direction.

backlog.spec: Make sure the loss is computed with a fused cross-entropy, and that the model uses torch.compile with mode default. If the logits softcap is computed in fp32 over the full vocab, compute it in bf16 and upcast only inside the cross-entropy. This should give a small throughput gain.

backlog.spec: Change the logit softcap constant (probably 15 or 30 in forward) to 15. If it is already 15, use 30.
backlog.title: Logit softcap 15

backlog.spec: Reduce the MLP hidden size from 4x to 3x model_dim. The saved compute is converted into more steps. Edit the c_fc/c_proj dims.
backlog.title: ReLU squared to SwiGLU-free tweak: MLP expansion 3x

backlog.spec: If value embeddings with gates exist, scale their gate init lower, or add them to every layer instead of alternating layers. Keep the change minimal.
backlog.title: Zero-init value-embedding gates scale

backlog.spec: Change the Muon momentum ramp (0.85 to 0.95) so that it finishes in 100 steps instead of 300, or set the final momentum to 0.97 during the stable phase.
backlog.title: Muon momentum warmup shorter

backlog.spec: Reduce the number of Newton-Schulz iterations in Muon from 5 to 4 to save time per step. Only do this if the code exposes ns_steps.

backlog.spec: Set the initial per-layer resid_lambdas to 0.9 rather than 1.0 and x0_lambdas to 0.2 instead of the current value. This changes the skip-connection mix at init.
backlog.title: Residual lambda init tweak

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine shape: lr_mult = 0.5*(1+cos(pi*progress_in_warmdown)) in the warmdown phase, keeping the WARMDOWN_RATIO of 0.5.
backlog.title: Time-based cosine warmdown

backlog.spec: Initialize the lm_head with std 0.001 rather than the current value, and token embeddings with std 0.5 rather than 1.0. This tests the init scale.
backlog.title: Untied embedding init std smaller

backlog.spec: Set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 32, which cuts the memory used and may improve speed by avoiding allocator pressure. Throughput can shift under torch.compile. Keep TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE unchanged.
backlog.title: Device batch 32 with accumulation

backlog.spec: Set DEPTH = 6 (model_dim = 6*64 = 384 rounded to a multiple of HEAD_DIM, so 384) and keep everything else. Fewer params and faster steps should give more optimizer steps in 300 s. If memory allows, set DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE = 128. Check that the model_dim computation still rounds to a multiple of HEAD_DIM 128.
backlog.title: Smaller model depth 6 with larger device batch

backlog.spec: Set TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE = 2**18 so each optimizer step uses 4 micro-steps fewer, doubling the number of optimizer updates in the fixed 300 s. Keep MATRIX_LR as is. In a short time budget, more steps usually beat larger batches. Make sure grad_accum_steps is computed from TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE and is an integer.
backlog.title: Halve total batch to 2**18 with device batch 64 and no accumulation tweaks

backlog.spec: In the training loop, for the first 25% of the time budget, use only the first half of each sequence (truncate inputs and targets to MAX_SEQ_LEN//2 along the time dimension, keeping the batch shape otherwise the same, or doubling the batch rows to hold token count constant). Then switch to full length. Shorter context is cheaper in attention and lets early training move faster. Be careful about torch.compile recompiling once at the switch; call it with dynamic=False and accept one recompile (compile time is not counted only at startup, so warm up both shapes before the timer starts if simple, otherwise skip warm-up).
backlog.title: Sequence-length curriculum (short then full)

backlog.spec: Maintain an exponential moving average of model parameters (decay 0.999, updated every step with torch._foreach_lerp_ in fp32 or bf16 copies) and swap the EMA weights into the model right before the final evaluation call, without touching the evaluation code itself. Begin EMA only after the warmdown starts to avoid early-weight bias. With a linear warmdown to zero the gain may be small, so use decay 0.995 if it lags.
backlog.title: EMA of weights for evaluation

backlog.spec: Replace the linear warmdown with a cosine shape: after the warmdown start (WARMDOWN_RATIO = 0.6), lr multiplier = FINAL_LR_FRAC + (1 - FINAL_LR_FRAC) * 0.5*(1+cos(pi*progress_in_warmdown)), with FINAL_LR_FRAC = 0.02. Keep the Muon momentum schedule as is.
backlog.title: Warmdown to non-linear cosine with 0.6 ratio and final LR 0.02

backlog.spec: In the training loop, compute the loss with label smoothing 0.05 (e.g. in the forward loss call if training, F.cross_entropy(..., label_smoothing=0.05)). Do not change the evaluation path or the loss used for evaluation; add a flag arg only used in training forward. Small regularization that can help calibration; if the model forward signature is shared with eval, add an optional parameter default 0.0 and pass 0.05 only from the training loop.
backlog.title: Label smoothing 0.05 on training loss only

backlog.spec: Replace the Muon momentum schedule (0.85 to 0.95 warmup) with a constant momentum of 0.9, and disable Nesterov in the Muon update if it is enabled (use the raw momentum buffer for orthogonalization). Tests whether the momentum scheduling matters.
backlog.title: Muon with Nesterov off and beta 0.9 constant

backlog.spec: Change the logit softcap from the current value (likely 15 to 30) to 30, and initialize lm_head weights with std 0.001 instead of the current value. Set UNEMBEDDING_LR = 0.006. Single combined change addressing the output layer's scale.
backlog.title: Untie lm_head init scale and raise UNEMBEDDING_LR jointly with softcap 30

backlog.spec: The model uses value embeddings, which add many parameters in embedding tables. Keep them only on the last 2 layers instead of alternating layers (or whatever the current pattern is) to cut the embedding parameters and memory traffic, and reduce optimizer work. Update has_ve(layer_idx, n_layer) accordingly. This is a bolder simplification that may raise throughput.
backlog.title: Remove value embeddings on alternating layers

backlog.spec: Add torch.nn.utils.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), 1.0) after the backward passes and before optimizer.step() in the training loop. It stabilizes early training with high LRs (EMBEDDING_LR 0.6, SCALAR_LR 0.5). If this costs measurable throughput, apply clipping every step anyway but with foreach=True (default).
backlog.title: Gradient clipping at 1.0

memo: Incumbent is mean_adjusted 1.0628 over 2 runs. Accepted so far: lm_head LR 0.008 (-0.0063), DEPTH 6 (-0.0286, tripwire flagged, so audit it), and TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2**18 (-0.0167, also tripwire flagged). Smaller models and more optimizer steps in 300 s helped. Bigger models hurt: depth 10 (+0.0214) and width 512 at depth 6 (+0.0207). Schedule changes all lost (warmup 0.03, warmdown 0.7, cosine), as did HEAD_DIM 64 (+0.0113) and the Muon momentum warmup of 100 steps (+0.0025). Muon LR 0.05 (-0.0008), label smoothing (-0.0010) and grad clipping (-0.0017) gave tiny gains and were rejected. The EMA run (slot 13) was invalid because it had no official score. Next: audit the tripwire flags. Try depth 4 or 5, and a smaller batch (2**17). Replicate the lambda init (-0.0034). Retry EMA only if it is simple. Skip schedule tweaks.
